messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> svc-api (prod, us-east-1) elevated 5xx rate (avg 12% in last 5m). Impact: gateway errors and timeouts. Pager: @maria oncall. Please ack and triage.

maria: acked. I'm looking at dashboards now. 5xx mix is mostly 502/504 from gateway -> inference-prod. Latency also spiking on tail.

maria: grabbing some logs from gateway; seeing a bunch of 'upstream reset' and 'connection failure' entries.

dan: I'm awake. Can you paste an example log line? My gut: retries or circuit breaker backpressure causing cascade.

maria: sample log: `"[envoy] upstream_reset: remote reset before response complete"` and `"upstream request timeout after 15s"` also a spike in upstream connect failures.

kevin: I pulled config history — there was an edge config push ~30m ago that changed route retry_policy (retries=2) and bumped per-cluster max connections thresholds. Might be related.

linda: Confirmed. Recent change: increased retries to reduce transient errors but that can amplify load on slow backends.

dan: If retries are causing amplification, disable them at gateway for svc-api and revert the route change. Also temporarily relax circuit breaker thresholds to avoid immediate cutoffs while we stabilize.

maria: will attempt disabling retries on the route. Applying a temporary override via Envoy config manager.

maria: command I'm running:
```bash
# patch route to disable retries
kubectl -n edge exec -it svc-edge-ctrl -- envoy-configctl patch-route svc-api --set "route.retry_policy.retry_on=\"none\""
```

ops-bot: Applying route override: svc-api retry_policy -> none (change-id: cfg-202603-9). Rolling to edge proxies.

ops-bot: Envoy config push complete to 75% of edges (canary). Monitoring.

maria: metrics update: 5xx dropped from 12% -> 6% within 30s after canary, still higher than normal but improving.

dan: good. Next step: reduce retry budget on the client side (inference callers) and reduce route weight to primary cluster to offload to fallback region while we investigate.

kevin: I'll update LB weights. Pushing a temp weight change: primary us-east-1 -> 70%, fallback us-west-2 -> 30%.

ops-bot: LB weight update applied (change-id: lb-202603-11). Routing shift live.

maria: after weight shift + disabling retries, 5xx now ~2.8% and tail latency improving. Still seeing intermittent 504s for a small subset of requests.

linda: I'm checking pod health; a subset of inference-prod pods show elevated accept queue length and worker timeouts. I'm scaling the deployment by +30% to absorb any backlog.

maria: `kubectl scale deploy/inference-prod --replicas=13 -n prod` -> scale started.

ops-bot: scale event accepted, new pods starting. ETA ~45s.

maria: customer impact snapshot: top affected customers keys: cust-analytics (heavy long-polling jobs), cust-chatbot (short requests). We'll notify CS for the impacted accounts after mitigation.

dan: For RCA, we'll look at why backends slowed — recent model shard rebalancer job ran ~40m ago? Could be GC/IO or model loading causing transient slowness. I'll pick this up.

kevin: also investigating whether circuit_breaker thresholds were too aggressive — config change log shows lowered max_pending_requests for cluster -> may have thrown healthy connections.

maria: handing off active incident to dan for root cause and postmortem. I'll stay on watcher for any regression. @kevin please follow up on LB/Envoy config audit.

dan: taking over. Creating incident record INC-2026-142, severity S1. Timeline & mitigation notes going into runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-142

maria: thanks everyone. Final status for now: customer impact reduced to low, mitigation in place (retries disabled, LB weights adjusted, pod scale), monitoring for 30m before marking mitigated.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-142 created and assigned to dan. Pager escalation suspended. If errors exceed threshold again, auto-page next oncall.
notes: temporary mitigations: disabled route retries, shifted LB weights, scaled inference-prod. Next actions: root cause analysis (model rebalancer/GC?), config audit, postmortem.
